subject: Question: how peering disruption should be reflected in availability tally
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@finsecure.com>, EdgeTransit Support <support@edgetransit.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-01-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Question: how peering disruption should be reflected in availability tally

Hi Sarah / EdgeTransit team,

Quick one from our side: on 2027-01-15 between ~01:45–03:10 UTC we saw a sustained increase in 5xxs and tail latency for requests routed to FinSecure's region. Network traces indicate intermittent BGP churn on the peering path and elevated egress latency from EdgeTransit POPs to our EU serving fleet.

We are preparing an availability reconciliation for FinSecure's Q4 usage and want to be explicit about how Redwood will apportion uptime/partial-degradation to third-party peering events versus our own runtime. Can you confirm:

- Whether EdgeTransit recorded an incident during that window (timestamped logs would be ideal)
- Whether FinSecure had any announced maintenance or scheduled BGP updates that morning

I attached a short trace export (peering-trace-20270115.csv) and a screenshot of latency percentiles (latency-samples-jan15.png).

Our SLA defines: "Third-party network outages that are out of Redwood's control may be considered for apportionment if corroborated with provider logs and cannot be reasonably mitigated." Please let us know what evidence you can share and whether you view this as a third-party attribution.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: peering-trace-20270115.csv (text/csv), latency-samples-jan15.png (image/png)

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@finsecure.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: ops@finsecure.com
Date: 2027-01-19T14:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Question: how peering disruption should be reflected in availability tally

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for flagging this. We saw elevated client-side errors during the same window. Our network team has pulled a short incident report — attaching finsecure-incident-report-20270115.pdf which includes our egress flow logs and the timestamps where our monitoring detected packet loss towards the EdgeTransit ASNs.

From our POV: we did not schedule any maintenance that morning and there were no config pushes on our side. The report suggests an external network issue between EdgeTransit and several downstream providers.

Happy to coordinate a joint review with EdgeTransit if you think it's helpful.

Best,
Sarah Li
Director of Infrastructure, FinSecure Inc.
sarah.li@finsecure.com

Attachments: finsecure-incident-report-20270115.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@finsecure.com>, EdgeTransit Support <support@edgetransit.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-01-20T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question: how peering disruption should be reflected in availability tally

On Tue, Jan 19, 2027 at 14:05 +01:00 Sarah Li <sarah.li@finsecure.com> wrote:
> Thanks for flagging this. We saw elevated client-side errors during the same window...

Thanks Sarah — I pulled the Redwood side telemetry for the window. Short summary:

- 01:40–02:05 UTC: sharp increase in SYN retransmits and a correlated +200–400ms p50/p95 for affected flows.
- 02:06–02:50 UTC: intermittent packet loss and path flaps; backend serving CPU remained stable.
- 02:50–03:10 UTC: partial recovery with periodic spikes.

Per our SLA apportionment guidance, we treat this as a partial degradation rather than a full outage. The key question for credit calculation is whether the root cause is attributable to a third-party transit provider (EdgeTransit) or to Redwood's network egress. If EdgeTransit can provide logs showing BGP flap / maintenance activity that overlaps the timestamps above, we would classify the affected minutes as third-party-impacted and apply apportionment.

If EdgeTransit disputes that classification, we will default to standard availability calculation and offer credits based on minutes of degraded service as measured by our production monitors.

Can EdgeTransit confirm whether they had any scheduled maintenance or observed BGP instability during 01:40–03:10 UTC?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com

Attachments referenced: extract of Redwood telemetry (included in Drive link)

From: EdgeTransit Support <support@edgetransit.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@finsecure.com>
Cc: --
Date: 2027-01-21T09:30:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Question: how peering disruption should be reflected in availability tally

Hi all,

Thanks for the report. We see a series of short-lived BGP withdraw/announce events across POPs that morning. We've attached the raw BGP session logs (edgetransit-bgp-flap.log) and our internal incident note. Preliminary timeline:

- 01:37–01:52 UTC: BGP churn affecting routes into our FRA/AMS POPs.
- 01:52–02:18 UTC: transient route instability, mitigations applied (route dampening, manual neighbor resets).
- 02:18–03:05 UTC: partial stabilization with occasional reroutes causing increased latency on specific paths.

We do have a standing maintenance window between 02:00–04:00 UTC for routine peering maintenance, but the churn we observed started before 02:00 UTC and correlates with a flapping neighbor in an upstream exchange. Given that the initial instability predates the scheduled window, we view at least the 01:37–01:52 UTC period as an unplanned third-party incident.

If Redwood's SLA requires strict corroboration, the attached logs should be sufficient to classify portions of the window as third-party impacted. Happy to jump on a call to align on minute-level apportionment if desired.

Regards,
EdgeTransit Support
support@edgetransit.io

Attachments: edgetransit-bgp-flap.log (text/plain)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@finsecure.com>, EdgeTransit Support <support@edgetransit.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-01-22T16:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question: how peering disruption should be reflected in availability tally -- request for formal apportionment

Sarah / EdgeTransit / team —

Appreciate the quick logs and timelines. To move this to a resolution for FinSecure's quarterly reconciliation, can the Redwood CS/legal team make a formal apportionment determination and propose the associated credit amount under the SLA?

Specifically we need:

1) A minute-level apportionment table showing which minutes are Redwood-impacted vs third-party-impacted vs undetermined.
2) The computed credit (tokens/minutes) per the contract formula for partial degradation.
3) A short statement we can include in the reconciliation packet indicating evidence used (EdgeTransit logs + FinSecure egress logs + Redwood telemetry).

Marissa / Monica — looping you in to finalize the apportionment and prepare the credit memo. If you need a joint call with FinSecure and EdgeTransit, propose a timeslot tomorrow morning UTC.

Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com
